title: Teach a step before an example uses it
statement: Teach every new step before a worked example uses it, because a worked example should put together only what is already known.
detail: A candidate BrainLift of the reading team on gradual release holds that worked examples assemble the known, so a novel step must be taught before it appears inside one (`grade3-reading/artifacts/team-direction-2026-09-09/research/02-current-brainlift-spov-audit.md`). The audit of the team's BrainLifts records it as borrowed from a general instruction framework and from a finding in a second round of review.
against: It is a borrowed rule; nothing in these sources measures it.

evidence.quote: Worked examples assemble the known — a novel step must be taught before it appears inside one.
The reader must never meet a structure mid-lesson that was never named.
